finding: Current transport evidence cannot safely prove that a failed request did not make remote progress in Notion. payload/account_pool.py records provider_call_entered=true and response_progress_observation_complete=false for current transport failures. payload/transport_evidence.py produces diagnostic hypotheses from curl code/timing/progress, not a typed proof of remote non-entry. Therefore V23 must remain fail-closed for current Notion TRANSPORT/httpx failures in durable Core mode; curl code or timing alone must not re-enable sibling retry.

safe_retry_rule.allowed_only_when: a lower layer emits an explicit typed proof that provider call was not entered / remote progress is impossible

exact_source_observations: AccountLease.run currently switches accounts for failover-class transport errors.
classify_transport returns hypotheses such as INDETERMINATE, SUPPORTED_BUT_NOT_PROVEN, REFUTED_FOR_SIMPLE_PRE_RESPONSE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT; none means remote request definitely did not progress.
V23 candidate v2 already provides a Core-only fail_closed_on_ambiguous_transport flag while preserving default NOTION_AGENT routing behavior.
product_decision: Do not add a heuristic availability exception to V23. If lower-level transport later exposes a typed pre-provider failure, add that type as the only safe exception and prove it separately before enabling sibling retry.
